events.title: Edward III Proclaimed King of England
events.description: After the deposition of his father Edward II by Queen Isabella and Roger Mortimer, the 14-year-old Edward III was proclaimed king of England. He was crowned on 1 February 1327.
events.significance: Edward III went on to reign for 50 years, launching the Hundred Years' War with France and strengthening Parliament's role in English government.

events.title: Henry VIII Secretly Marries Anne Boleyn
events.description: Henry VIII of England secretly married Anne Boleyn in a private ceremony, reportedly after she became pregnant with the future Elizabeth I. The marriage took place before his marriage to Catherine of Aragon had been formally annulled.
events.significance: The marriage accelerated the break with the Roman Catholic Church and the English Reformation, reshaping religious and political life in England.

events.title: Birth of Robert Burns
events.description: Robert Burns, the Scottish poet and lyricist, was born in Alloway, Ayrshire. He wrote in both Scots and English and collected and adapted traditional Scottish folk songs, including 'Auld Lang Syne'.
events.significance: Regarded as the national poet of Scotland, Burns is celebrated each year on Burns Night, and his work influenced Romanticism and liberal and socialist thought.

events.title: First Winter Olympic Games Open in Chamonix
events.description: The first Winter Olympic Games, originally called International Winter Sports Week, opened in Chamonix, France. Athletes from 16 nations competed in events such as skiing, skating, ice hockey and bobsleigh.
events.significance: The event began the Winter Olympics tradition, which was later recognized retroactively as the first Olympic Winter Games and grew into a major global sporting event.

events.title: Idi Amin Seizes Power in Uganda
events.description: Army commander Idi Amin led a military coup that overthrew President Milton Obote while Obote was attending a Commonwealth conference in Singapore.
events.significance: Amin's regime lasted until 1979 and was marked by severe human rights abuses, ethnic persecution, and economic collapse, with an estimated 100,000 to 500,000 deaths.
